ModMetaData.name: Guilt
ModMetaData.author: T&B Modding
ModMetaData.description:
The executions are yours. Your colonists carry them.
In the base game, ordering a prisoner executed costs the colonist who did it a small mood penalty for a few days, and then it is gone. Harvesting organs is much the same. Nothing accumulates. Nobody is ever changed by what you asked of them.
A conscience that keeps the account - Executions, organ harvesting, butchering people, selling prisoners, banishing someone to die and killing one of your own all leave a weight. - Doing a thing weighs far more than knowing it was done. - The weight fades slowly, about half over three or four weeks. It does not vanish. - As it builds: "something I did", then "things I've done", then "I don't recognise myself".
Can't look at them - A colonist who killed someone cannot be around that person's close family. The guilt points outwards as a lower opinion of the bereaved.
Confession - A colonist carrying enough will quietly tell someone they trust. It lifts a good share of the weight. - But now that person knows, and thinks less of them for a while. It is a real trade, not a free cure. - They never confess to the family of the person they wronged.
Callousing - Past a certain point a colonist stops feeling it. You get a letter when it happens, and a mark in their health tab. - They still know what they did. It no longer reaches them, and it will not reach them next time either.
Psychopaths and the bloodlusting never feel any of this. Neither do Sociopaths, for anyone outside their inner circle, if you run that mod.
This mod only changes how colonists feel. It never changes how anyone aims, works or chooses a job.
Requires Harmony. Safe to add to an existing save. RimWorld 1.6, no DLC needed.
